analysis: Both changed files are test-only (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/). No production source, trust-boundary code, crypto, attestation, or cache storage is modified, so no threat-model assets are weakened. EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift has a one-line change at line 313: the switch in the stream-recording helper now also ignores `.logprobs`. This tracks a new enum case in the server stream event type and has no security effect in test code. The head units I reviewed (lines 1811-2591) contain existing tests. They cover coordinator-path cacheScope/cacheSalt plumbing (TB-007/T-041: the tenant scope reaches the per-request salt), forged internal schema metadata rejection, media requests bypassing the bridge text path, cancellation propagation (T-010), and clamping of the heartbeat KV fallback reason. They also cover prefill-deadline and FCFS configuration. These tests reinforce the existing controls and make no behavioral changes. MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngineTests.swift adds a test (head lines 625-635) that pins `ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope` for GPT-OSS Harmony. It checks that client stop strings are scoped to the final channel, with the closers <|end|>, <|return|>, <|call|> and <|start|>, and that other models get nil. This is a test of production behavior, `ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope` and `CBv2StopStringScope`, that is supplied elsewhere in the PR and was not visible in this batch. The next review pass should examine that production code. Open questions: whether the stop-scope implementation could let consumer-supplied stop strings truncate or leak reasoning-channel content, and how the new `.logprobs` stream event is handled in production, i.e. whether logprob entries are encrypted along with the other response chunks (T-008). Neither can be assessed from the test-only changes seen here.
